inspection_summary: Inspected all 360 canonical logical lines of the four-page article. The source develops a conjectural bridge from logarithmically correlated critical-line zeta values, through CUE characteristic polynomials and random-energy partition functions, to freezing-law predictions for extremes, then reports preliminary zeta computations targeting the centering correction, limiting density, and free-energy plateau. The normalized text interleaves two print columns and contains formula-layout damage; in particular, four U+001C boundaries at logical lines 55, 63, 64, and 69 destroy relation signs, so the affected covariance/range fragments are quarantined and no exact inequalities are reconstructed.

accepted_units.title: Extreme critical-line values require a model beyond typical-value behavior
accepted_units.why_material: The text places the extreme-value question between broad known bounds and records an independence/normal baseline for local maxima, thereby isolating the modeling choice that the later correlation argument changes.
accepted_units.context_note: The normalized lines interleave the left-column zeta introduction with the right-column independence heuristic; both threads are source-visible, but their clauses must be read columnwise rather than as one paragraph.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (1) is layout-split, so the unit relies on the surrounding prose about the Euler product, critical line, and independent-Gaussian heuristic rather than reconstruction of the displayed formula.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line zeta values form a logarithmically correlated landscape
accepted_units.why_material: Selberg-type Gaussian behavior is supplemented by a two-point description whose prose-supported conclusion is logarithmic correlation with a small-scale saturation, explaining why extreme values need not follow an independent-sample model.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 50-62 define the random potential and averaging setup; lines 71-76 explicitly state the significance of the logarithmic form. Exact range inequalities in the intervening display are not used.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula dependent and scan verification needed: U+001C boundaries split lines 55/56, 63/64/65, and 69/70 and erase relation signs. The exact conditions in (3) are quarantined; only the independently stated prose-level logarithmic-correlation claim is accepted.

accepted_units.title: Random matrices and disordered landscapes provide a freezing hypothesis for zeta extremes
accepted_units.why_material: The article connects established zeta/random-matrix statistical analogies to logarithmically correlated energy landscapes and states the central strategic hypothesis that a low-temperature freezing transition governs characteristic-polynomial and, conjecturally, zeta maxima.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes the unresolved/numerically rare nature of zeta extremes and the source's explicit statement of how its single-matrix maximum question differs from earlier many-matrix tail work.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-supported; two-column extraction interleaves the historical RMT discussion with the freezing proposal but does not obscure the stated comparison.

accepted_units.title: CUE characteristic polynomials are scale-matched to critical-line zeta values
accepted_units.why_material: The characteristic polynomial supplies a tractable random-matrix surrogate, and matching CUE eigenvalue density with zeta-zero density aligns its Gaussian value scale with the zeta scale before any extreme-value transfer is attempted.
accepted_units.context_note: The right column begins the partition-function construction later isolated as d06; the local CUE definition and density identification are in the left-column clauses.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The determinant/product displays and variance typography are line-split. The construction and density-matching claim are recoverable from checked prose, but exact constants in the displayed normalization should be verified against the scan before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: A random Fourier representation exposes the CUE logarithmic covariance and microscopic cutoff
accepted_units.why_material: Representing the CUE log-characteristic polynomial by random Fourier modes makes logarithmic covariance explicit; finite matrix size saturates the singularity at the eigenvalue-spacing scale, yielding the structural match to the zeta-derived field.
accepted_units.context_note: The left-column Fourier/covariance argument is interleaved with right-column background on logarithmic random landscapes. The source itself states the small-distance logarithmic behavior, finite-N saturation, and the scale association.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (5) and the covariance display are extraction-fragile. The accepted mechanism follows the surrounding prose; exact coefficients and punctuation require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The maximum becomes a zero-temperature limit of a random-landscape free energy
accepted_units.why_material: Defining a positive-temperature partition function for the characteristic polynomial converts the maximum into the low-temperature limit of free energy, which is the operative bridge from extreme values to a freezing transition.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit intentionally overlaps d04-d05 because the normalized two-column page places the partition-function/free-energy argument in the right column alongside the CUE representation in the left. Lines 167-171 state the conjectural transfer to zeta.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed integrals and limit are visually fragmented but their semantic roles are explicitly described in prose. Exact normalizing factors should be scan-checked; the max/free-energy correspondence itself is source-supported.

accepted_units.title: CUE partition-function moments reduce to a Toeplitz/Selberg law
accepted_units.why_material: The source turns integer moments into Toeplitz determinants, applies their large-N asymptotics, and identifies a Dyson-Morris/Selberg-integral moment form matching a circular logarithmic landscape. This is the mathematical mechanism supporting transfer of the freezing result rather than analogy alone.
accepted_units.context_note: Page marker lines 176-179 and right-column numerical-introduction prose occur inside the span because of source layout. The derivation proceeds in the left-column clauses from the moment identity through (11).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula dependent. OCR obscures exponents and threshold typography near lines 210-231, so exact moment constants and convergence bounds are quarantined pending scan verification; the prose-stated Toeplitz-to-Selberg reduction and matching-form claim are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Freezing predicts a CUE maximum law distinct from short-range Gumbel behavior
accepted_units.why_material: Matching the moment form to the circular logarithmic model yields a centered/scaled maximum distribution, a 3/2 logarithmic correction, and a left-tail form that the source contrasts with the 1/2 correction and Gumbel density of short-range variables.
accepted_units.context_note: The left-column prediction is interleaved with right-column zeta numerical discussion. The explicit prose at lines 257-266 supplies the tail and 3/2-versus-1/2 comparison even where displayed fractions are degraded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (12)-(14) are line-broken and some fractions render as concatenated digits. The qualitative law, Bessel-density identification, tail statement, and constants stated unambiguously in prose are accepted; formula-level reuse needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The zeta mean-maximum correction favors logarithmic over short-range correlations
accepted_units.why_material: The first numerical diagnostic compares the distinct centering corrections predicted by logarithmic and short-range models; across the displayed heights the source reports that the 3/2 correction fits the sample means considerably better than 1/2.
accepted_units.context_note: Read the right-column clauses beginning at line 189 and continuing through Table I; the overlapping left column contains the independent moment derivation captured in d07.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The table entries and prose comparison are readable, but the model-mean display is typographically damaged. The accepted claim is the source's reported comparative fit, not a reconstructed formula or independent recomputation.

accepted_units.title: The zeta maximum-density test is supportive but explicitly inconclusive
accepted_units.why_material: The source compares normalized zeta maxima with the predicted density and tail, while explicitly recording slow convergence, omitted lower-order arithmetic terms, and the fact that the agreement does not conclusively verify the prediction.
accepted_units.context_note: The right-column numerical account is interleaved with the left-column CUE law. Its evidential limitation is part of the reusable unit, preventing preliminary agreement from being promoted to validation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The normalization display is broken across lines 243-251 and should not be reconstructed exactly from this text layer. The prose statements about the compared density, tail, omitted terms, and inconclusive status are readable.

accepted_units.title: A zeta partition function creates a direct freezing diagnostic
accepted_units.why_material: Rather than test only maxima, the source defines an integral of powers of critical-line zeta values over a fixed-length interval, making the inverse-temperature/free-energy behavior itself observable.
accepted_units.context_note: The computation and outcome resume after the page-four figures at lines 339-347; that separated continuation is captured in d12.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (14) is visually recoverable but line-split. Its semantic definition is supported by the introductory prose; exact normalization should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: The normalized zeta free energy exhibits the predicted freezing plateau
accepted_units.why_material: The source states the piecewise prediction that normalized free energy follows the high-temperature curve below the critical inverse temperature and remains constant above it, then reports numerical results consistent with that plateau after a lower-order correction.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 334-336 give the Figure 2 interpretation; lines 339-347 define the normalized free energy and state the prediction and reported agreement. Right-column bibliography is interleaved but mathematically irrelevant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The beta-dependent expressions are readable in prose/display but share lines with references and figure extraction. The qualitative breakpoint and plateau are accepted; exact plotting data and renormalization details require the original figure/scan.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Correlation-to-freezing mechanism chain
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source's reusable strategic chain is: expose logarithmic covariance, find a structurally matched CUE Fourier field, convert maxima to free energy, identify the partition moments with a circular logarithmic model, and transfer that model's freezing extreme law.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact covariance ranges and several moment constants are formula-unsafe in this extraction, and transfer from CUE to zeta remains explicitly conjectural.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Competing-correlation falsification ladder
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Short-range and logarithmic models are separated by multiple observables: the logarithmic centering correction, the non-Gumbel density/tail, and a low-temperature free-energy plateau, allowing the hypothesis to be challenged at more than one representational level.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The reported tests are preliminary, converge slowly, omit lower-order arithmetic effects in places, and are not independent validation of the proposed law.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Maximum statistics and thermodynamic behavior as complementary views
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Testing both normalized maxima and the beta-dependent partition free energy probes the same freezing proposal through an extreme-value view and a phase-transition view rather than relying on a single fit.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source provides numerical consistency only; figure extraction is incomplete and no claimed test is presented as conclusive.

within_source_saturation: All recoverable source-specific mechanisms, predictions, comparisons, and evidential limitations are represented. Further units would chiefly duplicate the abstract/conclusion, split routine algebra away from its moment-method role, select bibliography/plot coordinates, or depend on corrupted formula typography.
